findings.finding: 09ec admitted two SHA checks passing before either publication, then a successful later overwrite losing the first update. 2.0.2 requires the same atomic lock for all public writers and migration, full source revalidation while holding it, owner-token release, no PID/time-based stealing, and preservation of lock/old bytes/recovery information after partial publish. Manifest remains last; inconsistent packages fail closed.
findings.strongestAlternative: Single Coding Owner plus a pre-write SHA check is sufficient, or post-write reload can detect all conflicts.
findings.decision: Reject that explanation: two invocations by one Owner can race, and coherent overwrite reloads successfully. New serialization contract closes the specification counter. Implementation must exercise two real writers against the same source, stale input after lock acquisition, and injected partial-publication failure. No filesystem-wide atomicity or protection against arbitrary non-cooperating edits is claimed.
